source.citation: Moreau P, Karamanesht II, Domnikova N, et al. Pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic and covariate analysis of subcutaneous versus intravenous administration of bortezomib in patients with relapsed multiple myeloma. Clin Pharmacokinet 2012;51(12):823-829. doi:10.1007/s40262-012-0010-0
source.storage: Supplied by the platform owner; kept on her computer only, not committed.
source.extraction: AI-assisted. Table 1 values and quotes checked against the file text; Table 1 read from the layout text and the rendered page. Independent review pending.

relationship_to_model: Not used to build or fit the Lignet 2022 PK model (Hanley 2017 pediatric parameters scaled to adults; PK compared graphically with Reece 2011 only). MMY-3021 is a phase 3 study, not among the five phase 1 studies behind Kuan 2012. The CAN-1004 data in the same paper are already on the platform (bortezomib_pk_can1004_observed_v1.json) and are not used again here.

design.study: MMY-3021: randomized phase 3 study, subcutaneous versus intravenous bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4, 8 and 11 of 21-day cycles, relapsed multiple myeloma after 1-3 prior therapies; PK/PD substudy at selected sites.
design.arm_used: IV only (14 of 14 enrolled IV substudy patients assessable). The SC arm is not used: the model has no absorption step.
design.pk_day: Day 11 of cycle 1 only; no day 1 profile.

substudy.quote: a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic substudy, consisting of 32 patients (subcutaneous, n = 18; intravenous, n = 14), was conducted at selected sites

assessable.quote: In MMY-3021, 17 of 18 subcutaneous and 14 of 14 intravenous patients enrolled in the pharmacokinetic/ pharmacodynamic substudy at selected sites were assessable

auc_definition.quote: area under the plasma concentration–time curve (AUC) from time zero to the last quantifiable timepoint (AUClast)

table1_iv_day11.location: Table 1, MMY-3021, IV 1.0 mg/mL column, day 11 of cycle 1

limits: Day 11 only: the day 1 to day 11 rise cannot be assessed from this study.
Means and SDs only; no individual concentrations.
The assay's lower limit of quantification and the number of patients quantifiable at 72 h are not stated, so 'last quantifiable timepoint' may be earlier than 72 h for some patients.
